The Fifth Derivative of a Joint Score-Driven Filter

Source: R/gas_fifth.R
term_fifth.GasJoint.Rd

Computes the fifth derivative of the filtered predictors contracted against the caller's weights and three directions, with the lower orders' contractions along the same directions, through jets over every subset of the directions.

Usage

.gas_joint_fifth(
  term,
  psi,
  g,
  seed,
  blocks_data,
  directions,
  eta = NULL,
  sub = FALSE
)

Arguments

term

A built term.

psi

The term's parameters, named as term_params().

g

The weights, one column per filtered parameter.

seed

A list of one matrix of static rows per equation.

blocks_data

The model's derivative arrays, as set out above.

directions

A list of three numeric vectors, the directions \(v\), \(w\) and \(x\) in the caller's unknowns. The result is symmetric in the three.

eta

The static part of the predictor.

sub

Whether the members carry subformulas, whose charts are then read per observation.

Value

A list with jacobian, dphi, dpsi and domega, each with one element per filtered parameter (dphi and dpsi lists of three), and curvature.

Details

The levels' jets are sums of products of the chart's jets with the jets of earlier driving scores and levels, as at the lower orders of term_fourth(). The jet of each driving score is composed from the jets of the predictors of every equation by .gas_compose(), with the driving score's derivatives in those predictors given as data in blocks_data: filtered, u, U1, U2, U3, U4 as for the lower orders, and U5, an array with the observation, the driving score and five predictor indices.
